name: Open Line
designHypothesis: A shorter movement lane sharing a firing aperture makes screen state consequential. Gallery observation and reversible control remain useful; knowing the signal angle enables an alternate outcome without a tower visit.
population: Seven places, five retained defenders and four retained pickups. No map-area or population expansion.
modelScope: Deterministic actual C.move/C.step and swept projectiles, seed BELL-01, dt 1/90. No actor coordinates, health, equipment, timers or progress assigned. This is not a rendered playthrough or a human study.

hesitationProbe.method: Use the driver's live approach and ordinary release shot, then its central waypoints [0,-9],[0,-12],[0,-16]. Separately walk [-4,8.5],[-14,8.5],[-14,0],[-14,-11.5] without releasing the screen. In each case advance 450 unmodified C.step frames at dt 1/90 with the actual head at player position plus [0,1.65,0].
hesitationProbe.interpretation: Constant movement avoided damage on all three sampled approaches, but hesitation exposed a real danger in the open lane. This supports the intended observation/exposure contrast, not universal balance or measured player comprehension.

recoveryFindings.finding: The first Returning Bell check expected returning-bell-1 although the correct fresh preview is returning-bell-2. It failed before gameplay with no captured runtime errors. The expectation was corrected; authentic v1 checkpoint restore remains separately tested.

The first recovered local full suite had 198 passing tests and one release-version mismatch: core was 0.15.0 while release/roadmap were still 0.14.0. Metadata and artifact-authored workbook were synchronized without changing original task statuses or gates.
A local run started before OPEN-LINE.md was written failed its evidence-path check. After assembly, all 199 model tests passed. The failed intermediate run is not credited as acceptance.
Local Chromium navigation to the loopback test server was blocked by the execution environment. It is not a gameplay pass. Native browser acceptance is performed in GitHub Actions.

remainingEvidence: At this record's creation, rendered route/XR/save journeys and public publication verification were still pending. Their eventual outcomes belong in the separate publication receipt, not in these model observations.
limits: Human first/repeat-play understanding, comfort, sustained performance, real Xbox/Quest devices and final art/audio remain open. The Architect's Table is discovery-limited authored-chapter inspection, not room scanning, physical anchoring or hand-only combat.
nextOpportunity: Observe whether unfamiliar players notice the release, predict the exposed lane, recover from a miss or blocked approach and exploit the signal angle on replay before adding another chapter.
